newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong activists call off Diaoyu voyage.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong activists call off Diaoyu voyage.

text.p: A group of Hong Kong activists said on Tuesday that a shortage of funds and pressure from the Taiwanese government had forced them to postpone a protest voyage to the disputed Diaoyu islands in the East China Sea.

Spokesman Albert Ho told a news conference that fishing boat captains in Taiwan had backed out of Sunday's planned trip because the group of some 60 campaigners could not afford deposits sought as insurance against damage and arrest by Japanese authorities.
"The Japanese government has repeatedly warned that this time they are going to seize the boat, arrest the people and take them to prosecution," Ho said.
The chain of islands is claimed by China, Taiwan and Japan.

The group said the Taiwanese government also pressured fishermen who would have agreed to take them to the isles, apparently upset over a trip last year when activists planted a mainland Chinese flag on the isles.

Last October, the activists together with Taiwan campaigners broke through a Japanese maritime cordon, went ashore on one of the islands and hoisted the flags of China and Taiwan in a bid to assert China's sovereignty over the rocky outcrops.
"Taiwanese government is taking the fishermen to task for letting people plant the flag of mainland China on Diaoyu," Ho said.
The activists said they would now try to stage a protest in Japan.
Ho said they would also try to raise enough money to buy their own boat to sail to the islands later.

"We need money, and we will be making our best endeavour in the month to come to raise money such that I hope maybe in August, maybe in October, maybe in September, we can make another attempt to the Diaoyu Islands," he said.
Emotions are running high in Hong Kong over the disputed Diaoyu, or Senkakus as they are known in Japan.

During the past week, provoked by a landing on the islands by a group of Japanese nationalists, Hong Kong activists have staged fresh protest marches and demonstrations outside Japan's consulate in the territory.
The cluster of islands ignited fiery nationalist passions in Chinese communities in Hong Kong and Taiwan last year after a Japanese rightist group built a lighthouse there.

At the high point of the 1996 protests, a Hong Kong activist, David Chan, was drowned during a dramatic attempt to land on the islands. His death drew tens of thousands of mourners and protesters on to the streets of Hong Kong.

A group of Hong Kong activists stormed into the Japanese consulate last year to protest over Tokyo's claims to a disputed island chain. Three of them were convicted of unlawful assembly on Monday and fined HK$4,000 (US$516) each.
